findings.F1: The short side is what keeps the book from paying. On 7,684 active short bars the mean move in the position's direction is −0.080 %, against +0.368 % on 7,918 long bars. Rebuilt with the shorts set flat, the book (an approximation: allocation × next-day return, minus 0.11 % per unit of turnover) clears both failed measures: mean daily return 0.000617 against 0.000488 for all bars, Calmar 1.25 against 0.49, Sharpe 1.02 against 0.60, deepest fall −17.8 % against −29.2 %. The shorts alone have a mean of −0.000082, a Sharpe of −0.15 and a deepest fall of −50.1 %.
findings.F2: Short losses come from falling coins whose volatility is high. Shorts in the top quartile of 30-day daily volatility move −0.517 % per day in their direction (t −3.12, n 1,452). Shorts in the three lower quartiles move between +0.09 % and +0.14 % (t about 0.9 each).
findings.F3: The same reversal grows with volatility against the coin's own recent level, measured as 30-day volatility over its 60-day median. In falling coins the next-day move in the short's direction falls steadily across the quartiles: +0.329 % (t 2.70, n 1,363), −0.070 %, −0.003 %, then −0.773 % in the top quartile (t −3.38, n 718).
findings.F4: Rising coins keep rising at every volatility level, and most strongly when volatility is high against its own past. Longs in the top relative-volatility quartile move +0.724 % (t 4.06, n 1,659), and longs in the top absolute-volatility quartile move +0.507 % (t 2.80).
findings.F5: The book's worst periods are years with a large short share. In 2018 longs were 17 % of active bars and the move in the position's direction was −0.155 %. In 2025 longs were 37 % and the move was −0.005 %. In 2020 longs were 75 % and the move was +0.307 %.
findings.F6: Costs are not the main problem.

ideas.idea: In a coin whose 30-day net move has been large relative to its 30-day high-low range, the larger its 30-day return, the further the coin moves in that same direction over the next day, only while that 30-day return is a rise.
ideas.consequence: A trader would follow a coin's 30-day trend upward for the next day, scaled by the size of the rise, and would not short a coin's 30-day fall.
ideas.name: uptrend continues next day

ideas.idea: In a coin whose 30-day net move has been large relative to its 30-day high-low range, the larger its 30-day return, the further the coin moves in that same direction over the next day, except after a 30-day fall, where the higher its 30-day volatility against its own last 60 days, the more the coin rises over the next day.
ideas.consequence: A trader would follow a coin's 30-day rise, and would buy rather than short a coin that is falling while volatile against its own past, more so the higher that volatility.
ideas.name: volatile downtrends rebound next day

ideas.idea: In a coin whose 30-day net move has been a large fall relative to its 30-day high-low range, the higher its 30-day daily volatility against its own median of the last 60 days, the more the coin rises over the next day.
ideas.consequence: A trader would buy a steadily falling coin whose volatility has jumped against its own past, sized by how far it has jumped, expecting a rebound the next day.
ideas.name: volatile selloff next-day rebound
